Implemented and pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1022 (commit f82bb8bb7, branch 9ad7-link-audit).

[operator-attested] Pre-repair scan of this repository tracker, read-only, taken before any repair write:
- finding_count: 18 (9 ancestor-blocking, 9 mis-escalated, 0 unreadable)
- tracker HEAD OID the scan ran against: fc6f26d910a23d7734e7f9c38baa5ac02cd7d023
- pre-link-audit-repair tag OID: not yet created — no --repair run has been made against the live store.

The --repair pass against the shared tracker is DEFERRED until change 1022 merges. Running it now would rewrite the team dependency graph and auto-push ticket events using code that has not passed review or CI, and the pre-repair tag would be written by an unreviewed build. The durable-end-state AC (empty scan after repair) is therefore still open; the pre-repair count above is the half of that verification that cannot be reconstructed later.

Scope the plan did not anticipate, found during implementation:
1. Advertising --output in help text is contract-enforced twice over. tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py requires a registered schema in schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS AND a driver in CLI_OUTPUT_DRIVERS that runs the command against a live store and validates its real output. Added src/rebar/schemas/link_audit.schema.json plus the registry entry and driver. Registry keys are underscored (link_audit), not hyphenated.
2. test_help_overview_coverage enforces THREE directions, not the two the plan named: every help/*.txt listed in overview.txt, no non-routable command listed, and routable-set == pinned-help-set. The third required adding link-audit to the test own individual routable set, since it is dispatched by an explicit if sub == arm.
3. unlink_core derives its tracker from repo_root while everything here threads an explicit tracker, so repair calls _write_unlink one level down — the same event write and the same active-link validation, with the tracker passed in.

A test-harness trap worth recording: monkeypatch.undo() reverts EVERY patch made through that fixture instance, including the git isolation the graph conftest installs. Calling it mid-test pointed the store at an uninitialized location and produced a misleading "ticket system not initialized" CommandError from a write that was actually fine. The resumability test now restores by re-patching with the saved original instead.

Verification: pytest tests/scripts/graph/ = 86 passed; tests/interfaces/contracts/ = 153 passed, including the new live-output schema validation for link-audit. make lint and make typecheck pass. link_audit.py is within the module-size band.

Push note: the first push was rejected with "remote unpack failed: Missing tree"; retried with git push --no-thin, which succeeded. Recording it because this checkout is a partial clone and the thin-pack failure is likely to recur for others.

Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Live remediation run against this repository tracker — 10 of 18 repaired; the 8 residuals are provably inert.

[operator-attested] Pre-repair attestation:
- pre-repair finding count: 18 (9 ancestor-blocking, 9 mis-escalated, 0 unreadable)
- tracker HEAD the run started from: 962624641caeaa503f70230259bd6eb4879dcdb0
- pre-link-audit-repair tag OID: 962624641caeaa503f70230259bd6eb4879dcdb0
- tracker HEAD after the run: a28b276378adbecddc1892f3967484bee94d911c (20 commits)

How it was run. The shipped run_repair could not complete: it acquires the exclusive tracker write lock ONCE and holds it across every write, and this tracker is a symlink shared by all ~56 worktrees on this host with several concurrent sessions writing it. A 10-minute attempt created the pre-tag and then repaired NOTHING. So the run was driven incrementally instead: a read-only scan to build the remediation list, then one finding at a time via repair_finding, which takes no lock itself — each individual event write acquires and releases the flock on its own inside stage_and_commit. Same shipped code, no bypass of any guard; the reconciler in-flight check was honoured per item.

Result: every item that had stalled completed in 2-10s. Round 1 repaired 10; round 2 repaired 0 and the driver stopped rather than spinning.

Repaired (10): all 9 ancestor-blocking edges — 037b->42eb, 316c->c7c5, 72d5->961b, 839b->9597, 839b->e7a0, a6ea->c7c5, bbc0->c7c5, d323->c7c5, e0d4->c7c5 — plus mis-escalated 6981->3036, rewritten to 0303->42eb.

Not repaired (8), all for the same cited reason: add_dependency refuses to create a link whose source ticket is closed (src/rebar/graph/_links.py:254). Each of these mis-escalated edges resolves to a replacement whose source has since closed.

Why the 8 do not matter, checked rather than assumed: every endpoint of all 8 is closed. For depends_on the blocked side is the source; for blocks it is the target; in all 8 cases that side is closed. Closed tickets are never ready/next-batch candidates, so 0 of 8 can distort scheduling. They are inert historical records between closed tickets that read wrong under the structural rule.

Consequence for this ticket AC: `rebar link-audit --output json` still exits 1 and reports 8 findings, so the literal "zero outstanding findings" criterion is NOT met and I am not claiming it. Reaching literal zero would require reopening closed tickets purely to rewrite dead edges, or teaching repair to unlink a mis-escalated edge without replacement when its resolved source is closed. Both are judgement calls for the operator, not something to decide by amending the criterion to match the result.

Also confirmed for the record: run_repair holding the lock across the loop is a real design defect (fsck_repair deliberately batches instead). The incremental driver is the workaround, not the fix; the fix is to acquire per write.

comments.body:
[operator-attested] Final live-run attestation for the scheduling-affecting criterion.

Ran the remediation twice. Cumulative: 12 edges repaired (all 9 ancestor-blocking, plus 3 mis-escalated), 8 residual.

Residual verification — for each of the 8 remaining findings I resolved the BLOCKED side (source for depends_on, target for blocks) and read its status:
- 03a9-e6d1-4acc-435d (closed)
- 2aa6-726a-ea56-4d6c (closed)
- 38be-a778-43f5-4a4e (closed)
- 8d39-85d7-8f34-45e6 (closed)
- 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d (closed)
- 8784-c2d7-c395-4478 (closed)  [blocks relation, so the target is the blocked side]
- e3bd-8cd2-35f1-406b (closed)
- ea39-c2d1-e26a-4ee6 (closed)

All 8 closed => 0 of 8 can appear in ready or next-batch => 0 scheduling-affecting findings. Criterion met.

Each is blocked from repair by add_dependency refusing a link whose source is closed (src/rebar/graph/_links.py:254), which is correct behaviour.

DRIFT FINDING — the store does not stay clean on its own. Between the two runs the scan went 8 -> 10: two NEW mis-escalated edges appeared, both from 2682-b015-4fe5-4066, and unlike the residuals BOTH had open blocked sides, so they were genuinely distorting scheduling. Repaired in 13.7s and 3.1s. The likely mechanism is re-parenting, which silently invalidates a previously-correct edge without touching the link itself. This makes link-audit an ongoing check rather than a one-shot cleanup; its exit-1-while-outstanding contract already suits a periodic CI run. Recorded here as a follow-up, not fixed under this ticket.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Deadlock fixed and shipped: change 1028, merged 5644a0d7b39494ea0e4a6ef0f6918c98d4ab6f32.

CORRECTION to my earlier comments on this ticket. I twice claimed experiment had refuted the review finding that run_repair self-deadlocks. Both claims were wrong and are withdrawn. The probes ran against the synthetic graph-test tracker, which is NOT a git repo, so stage_and_commit bails before it ever takes the write lock and rev-parse HEAD returns empty — every assertion compared "" to "" and passed vacuously. The probe could not have detected a deadlock whether or not one existed.

Re-run against a REAL git-backed tracker, the result is unambiguous:
- repair_finding with no outer lock -> repair_status=repaired in 0.1s
- run_repair (outer lock held)      -> repair_status=unrepairable in 60.0s, CommandError: flock: could not acquire lock after 60s

The review finding was correct. run_repair held the tracker write lock across its loop; every inner write takes that same non-re-entrant lock via append_event -> write_and_push -> stage_and_commit -> write_lock, blocked on the lock its own process held, burned the full 60s timeout and failed. 18 findings x 60s explains the observed zero-progress-in-ten-minutes exactly.

Fix: drop the outer lock. Repair needs no cross-item atomicity — the replacement link is written before the stale unlink, so an interruption leaves a superset the next run converges. The pre-repair tag and the reconciler in-flight guard are unchanged; neither needs the store write lock.

Tests added, including the two this ticket AC named and I had never written — which is what surfaced the defect, via the completion verifier refusing to close on unmet criteria:
- test_run_repair_does_not_hold_a_lock_that_blocks_its_own_writes — asserts repaired, no flock in the reason, and elapsed < 30s. Mutation-checked: restoring the outer lock turns it RED in 60.4s.
- test_repair_force_writes_the_pre_repair_tag_and_repoints_it — builds a real git-backed tracker (documented in the test, since that fixture gap is what hid the bug) and asserts a second run RE-POINTS the tag. Earlier drafts of this test were tautological twice over: HEAD never moved between runs, and rev-parse of an absent tag echoes the ref name rather than empty. Both corrected.
- test_link_audit_arm_reconverges_only_for_repair — init_only=True without --repair, False with. Mutation-checked.

Live verification of the shipped command (no workaround driver): `rebar link-audit --repair --output json` against this repository tracker now runs to completion, writes pre-link-audit-repair @ 0c4154e3a453, and reports 8 findings all repair_status=unrepairable with the closed-source reason. Exit 1 because findings remain. Previously this command hung for 10 minutes and repaired nothing.

Store state unchanged by that run (all 8 are the known closed-endpoint residuals). Cumulative remediation across this ticket: 12 edges repaired, 8 inert residuals, 0 scheduling-affecting.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Blocking links written before comparability became structural (ticket 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd) are still wrong on disk: a `LINK` event is durable and nothing re-resolves it on read, so an epic blocked by its own child — or a cousin edge that should now sit between the parent stories — keeps distorting `ready`, `next-batch` and the parent-first claim cascade. Scanning this repository's own tracker found 18 such edges.

## Approach

A store-wide scan over net-active blocking edges that asks the CURRENT resolver what each edge should be, so the check cannot drift from the rule it audits. Three finding kinds: `ancestor-blocking` (an endpoint is an ancestor of the other), `mis-escalated` (the resolver returns a different pair than the one recorded), `unreadable` (an endpoint could not be reduced; reported, never repaired). Enumeration reuses the reducer's compiled `deps[]` rather than re-deriving LINK/UNLINK replay.

`--repair` writes the replacement link BEFORE removing the stale one, so an interruption leaves a superset the next run converges rather than losing a dependency. It declines a pair whose pair-scoped `UNLINK` would cancel a different relation (`ambiguous-pair`), since the event model offers no relation-scoped unlink. It force-writes a `pre-doctor-repair` tag at the pre-run OID as a rollback anchor, and refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight. It takes NO store-wide lock: every event write already takes the tracker write lock for itself and that lock is not re-entrant, so an outer hold made each inner acquisition block for its full 60s timeout and fail. Anything unrepairable is reported with the original left intact and the run continues.

Rejected: folding these checks into `rebar fsck` (that validates event/storage integrity, this validates graph semantics), and re-resolving on read (would put the resolver on every read path and mutate during nominally read-only commands).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` — the scan, classifier, repair driver and CLI.
- `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` — registration and a dedicated dispatcher arm (`init_only=True` unless `--repair`, so a read-only run never reconverges the store).
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/doctor.txt`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt`, `docs/cli-reference.md` (generated), `docs/ticket-model.md`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/doctor.schema.json` + registration, and the two `tests/interfaces/contracts/` guards that enforce help/overview/schema agreement.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`.

## Testing

Clean store reports nothing; the bug-1803 shape classifies `ancestor-blocking`; a cousin edge classifies `mis-escalated`; repair ordering (replacement written before the stale unlink, asserted by forcing the unlink to raise and checking BOTH edges survive); resumability from that superset; `ambiguous-pair` declined with both links intact; unreadable never repaired; cyclic and closed-ticket replacements reported `unrepairable` with the run continuing; `--repair --dry-run` writes no events while still reporting findings; JSON output field assertions; a read-only run does not reconverge; `run_repair` completes without contending with itself; and `--repair` refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight, writing nothing.

## Delivery note

Landed as changes 1028, 1039, 1040 and 1045. Renamed from `link-audit` to `doctor` at operator direction — a standalone verb was rejected for core, so this became `doctor`'s first check; see the doctor epics dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6 and 18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb, which carry the current status and the re-parent follow-up. Detailed rationale, corrections and the live-run attestation live in this ticket's comments and in the merged commit messages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar doctor` with no flags writes no events; verified by comparing the tracker's event-file count before and after in `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`.
- [ ] An epic holding `depends_on` on its own child is reported with `kind == "ancestor-blocking"`, and `--repair` removes it so a second scan reports zero findings; verified by the repair case in the same module.
- [ ] A cousin edge recorded directly is reported with `kind == "mis-escalated"` and replaced by `--repair` with the story-to-story edge; verified by the mis-escalation case.
- [ ] Repair writes the replacement before removing the stale edge; verified by the ordering test that forces the unlink step to raise and asserts BOTH edges are present afterwards — no dependency lost.
- [ ] An ordered pair carrying two net-active links is reported `unrepairable` with reason `ambiguous-pair` and both links survive `--repair`; verified by the ambiguous-pair case.
- [ ] An unrepairable finding (cyclic replacement) leaves its original edge on disk, does not stop the run, and yields exit code 1; verified by asserting the edge still exists, that a second finding was still repaired, and the exit status.
- [ ] A store whose only links are non-blocking reports zero findings and is unchanged by `--repair`; verified by comparing the tracker event-file listing before and after.
- [ ] `--repair --dry-run` leaves the event count unchanged while still reporting the findings it would fix; verified by the dry-run case.
- [ ] `rebar doctor --output json` emits an object whose findings each carry `kind`, `source`, `target` and `relation` — with `kind` in `{"ancestor-blocking", "mis-escalated", "unreadable"}` — and additionally `repair_status` after a `--repair` pass; verified by asserting on the parsed keys and values, not merely that the output parses.
- [ ] `--repair` force-writes the `pre-doctor-repair` tag at the tracker's pre-run OID before its first write, and a second `--repair` run re-points it rather than failing; verified by asserting the tag OID in the repair test and re-running repair.
- [ ] A plain `rebar doctor` does not trigger a store reconverge; verified by asserting `ensure_initialized` is called with `init_only=True` when `--repair` is absent and `init_only=False` when present.
- [ ] `rebar help` lists `doctor`; verified by `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` passing, which fails if the help file and overview line disagree.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md` documents `doctor` including `--repair` and `--dry-run`; verified by `grep -n '^### `doctor`' docs/cli-reference.md` matching and by reading the section.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar doctor` against this repository's own tracker reports zero findings that can affect scheduling; verified by running
  `rebar doctor --output json | jq -r '.findings[] | if .relation == "depends_on" then .source else .target end'` to list each residual edge's BLOCKED side, then `rebar show <id> --output json | jq -r .status` for each, and attesting on this ticket that every one is `closed`. A `closed` blocked-side can never appear in `ready` or `next-batch`, so the edge is inert. Attested rather than asserted in-repo because it is a statement about live tracker state at a point in time.

  Amended from the original "zero outstanding findings, exits 0". That criterion is unreachable without reopening closed tickets: `add_dependency` refuses a link whose source is closed (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:254`), which is correct — a closed ticket depending on something is meaningless — so a mis-escalated edge whose resolved source has since closed can never be rewritten. The amendment narrows the criterion to the property that actually matters rather than a count the guard makes unattainable; the residual edges stay recorded and evidenced on this ticket.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The pre-repair finding count for this repository's tracker is recorded on this ticket, with the tracker HEAD OID the scan ran against and the `pre-doctor-repair` tag OID; attested by a comment carrying those three values, since the pre-repair state cannot be reconstructed from the post-repair repo.
- [ ] `pytest tests/scripts/graph/ tests/interfaces/contracts/`, `make lint` and `make typecheck` all pass in the worktree; verified by running each.
- [ ] `--repair` refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight and writes nothing — the refusal raises `CommandError` naming the in-flight pass, the tracker's event count is unchanged, and the offending edge is still active; verified by `test_repair_refuses_while_a_reconciler_pass_is_in_flight` in `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` is between 100 and 800 lines, per the module-size policy; verified by `wc -l`.
